name: go2_shadow_walk
title: Go2 walk (SHADOWING: certified ghost + corridor + GHOST-FF)
summary: The Unitree Go2 walks by SHADOWING a certified achievable ghost -- the same method the G1 flagship uses, now carried onto a quadruped. This is the skill that makes the quads' `method: shadowing` label TRUE: it has a real stored ghost lut, a recorded gate verdict, and a corridor-bounded residual, where the legacy `go2_walk` skill has a generated trot retarget and no validator. Head-to-head on the live deploy ruler (3x240 s per side, interleaved, same pod/world/physics): 0.429 vs 0.381 m/s (+12.6%), lateral drift 0.05 vs 0.26 m (5x straighter), 0 falls on both sides.

ghost.format: json lut (nb=64 bins, 12 joints, freq 1.8 Hz, vx 0.3775)
ghost.provenance: recorded/achieved (doctrine class 1a) -- the LEGACY champion's OWN achieved gait, rolled deterministically on the deploy-matched MJCF (kp=250/kv=6, 16 ms x 8 substeps), steady segment phase-folded at 64 bins and harmonic-smoothed. The incumbent, certified.
ghost.validator: PASS (stamped into the lut, 2026-07-13: all 8 gates ok against the REAL go2.urdf). Until then this read 'ghost_validator.py's T0 limit check reads the G1 URDF and is VACUOUS for a quad' -- and it was: an unregistered robot skipped every model-aware gate and still printed PASS. The registry now knows the Go2, the validator FAILS CLOSED when it does not know a robot, and it pairs mirror joints by name (FL<->FR), so the lut no longer has to carry fake humanoid joint aliases to be checked. The builder's own binding gates remain in the lut's `gates` key: lut_replay (the folded lut + its feedforward, tracked by the bare deploy-grade PD with NO crane, WALKS: 0.382 m/s, peak torque 0.976 of limit), construction_reroll (3.94 m, no fall), support_fwp_certificate_replay (base_frac95 0.0743).
ghost.corridor_law: ghost peak |ctrl - q| = 0.217 rad at kp=250, which EXCEEDS the 0.15 corridor -- so the reference is untrackable by corridor alone BY CONSTRUCTION. GHOST_FF=1 is therefore MANDATORY for this skill: the declared feedforward shifts the corridor centre and the 0.15 residual only has to supply corrections. Training and deploy both set it.

obs.notes: UNCHANGED from the legacy trainer -- the ghost enters via the clock, the corridor and the reward, not via new obs.

policy.warmstart: gpu_go2_walk_main/warmstart.pt -- DISCLOSURE: the champion is FINE-TUNED FROM THE LEGACY CHAMPION'S WEIGHTS under the ghost corridor, not trained from scratch. The head-to-head is therefore an honest comparison of the two DEPLOYED POLICIES, and an honest demonstration that Shadowing UPGRADES an incumbent -- it is NOT a from-scratch method-vs-method comparison.

baton.notes: Phase-clocked and periodic, so it is a legal BATON leg. A quad BATON sequence (walk -> turn -> walk) additionally needs a go2_turn skill, which does not exist yet.

train.env: QUAD_GHOST=<lut> QUAD_GHOST_FF=1 QUAD_W_GMATCH=2.0 QUAD_RES_SCALE=0.15 QUAD_ENVS=16384 QUAD_FAST_RESET=1 MPC_NJMAX=64 MPC_NCONMAX=64 QUAD_ITERS=400
train.notes: Ghost mode is strictly opt-in: with QUAD_GHOST unset the trainer returns the unmodified legacy env class, so legacy training is byte-identical. Trained on the 5.92x fast path: RunPod RTX 4090, QUAD_ENVS=16384 + QUAD_FAST_RESET=1 + MPC_NJMAX/NCONMAX=64 (the `env` field above). Measured throughput for THAT EXACT CONFIG is 727,583 env-steps/s cumulative over a full 400-iteration run (the 783,582 peak is a single windowed sample at it=40; the 5.92x is vs the 132,362 same-window baseline at QUAD_ENVS=4096) (measured on the training pod; the run record is held with the ops tree and is not part of the public snapshot). Unit: one env-step = one 16 ms CONTROL step = 8 physics substeps; do not compare it to a raw physics-step rate. The rate is a property of (GPU, K, flags), NOT of this skill: the same in-engine trainer measures 10,228 env-steps/s at K=256 on a laptop RTX 3060 (OmniBench lane-2 tier C, docs/benchmarks/omnibench-2026-07-24.md). An earlier version of this note read '~780k env-steps/s' with no batch or machine attached.

deploy.notes: Identical scene/physics to go2_walk_deploy.omniworld -- ONLY the controller line differs, which is what makes the head-to-head fair. No harness: quads carry no crane.

verification.venue: RunPod RTX 4090, interleaved S/L, 3x240 s wall per side (~1600 s sim each)
verification.result: SHADOWING 0.429 m/s / 0 falls / |y|max 0.05 m / gmatch 0.864 vs LEGACY 0.381 m/s / 0 falls / |y|max 0.26 m. Speed +12.6%, drift 5x better, durability tied (neither ever fell).
honest_caveats: Deploy is DETERMINISTIC: the 3 runs per side are reproducibility checks, not independent samples (shadow scored 0.429 m/s on every single run). Distances differ only in how much sim time the wall window bought.
Legacy reproduced its own documented Table A record (87.5 m / 0.380 m/s vs documented 86.7 m / 0.379) -- the baseline was NOT handicapped.
Trade-off: shadow rides ~2 cm lower (body_z 0.272 vs 0.292) and rolls slightly more (|roll| 0.095 vs 0.069 mean).
The champion is warm-started from the legacy champion (see policy.warmstart).
verification.voided_first_attempt: An earlier exam produced a MUCH larger apparent win (640 m vs 411 m) and was INVALID: onnxruntime was missing from the controller interpreter, so BOTH sides silently ran with ZERO residual and exited 0. See docs + the fail-loud fix in the deploy controllers.
